title: Add multi-instance support: one container per workspace
body:
# Multi-instance support: one container per workspace

## Why

`gp-pi` was one long-lived container with one shared `gp-pi-home` volume and
an optional workspace at `/work`. Docker fixes bind mounts at container
creation, so changing the workspace meant destroying the container and killing
every running agent, and once a workspace was mounted every agent session in
the one container could read every other session's mount. A notes instance
sharing a container with a code instance is not isolation.

This makes an instance per workspace while keeping one login and one shared
config. It is deliberately light isolation: mount isolation plus per-instance
agent state, with credentials shared.

## Design

**Bare `gp-pi` is mountless.** The default instance is the historical `gp-pi`
container with a disposable `/work`. Bare `gp-pi`, `gp-pi attach`, `gp-pi up`
and `gp-pi auth` attach to an existing instance whose recorded workspace
contains the cwd, and otherwise ensure the mountless default instance. The
create path mounts neither `GP_PI_WORKSPACE` nor a cwd-derived workspace, so
the sandbox boundary is what it always was unless a mount is asked for.

**The mount is explicit: `gp-pi --workspace [dir]`.** It mounts `dir` at
`/work`, defaulting to the cwd's workspace root, and attaches to or creates
the derived named instance. Inside a git repository the workspace root is the
repository's main worktree, not a `.worktrees/...` path, so two agents in two
worktrees of one repo share an instance. The flag is idempotent: a second run
for the same workspace attaches rather than creating another instance.
`gp-pi --no-workspace` is the explicit mountless form and takes the same
create path as bare `gp-pi`. `gp-pi new <name> --workspace <dir>` names an
instance directly.

This reverses the first cut of multi-instance, which had bare `gp-pi` resolve
the cwd and auto-create a mounted instance. That turned the mount on by
default in practice, which contradicted the "off by default" posture in
`docs/design.md`, so the default is mountless again and the mount is a
per-invocation flag. The original reasoning for both the mount and one
container per workspace is kept in `docs/design.md`, with the reversal
recorded next to it.

**Shared credentials, per-instance state.** `gp-pi-home` stays at `/home/pi`
and holds `.ssh`, `.aws`, `.config/gh`, `.gitconfig` and `.pi/agent` with
`auth.json` and `settings.json`. `gp-pi-state-<name>` is mounted at
`/home/pi/.state`, shadowing that subdirectory, and holds pi sessions, herdr
sessions and the `gp-delegate` registry. `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_STATE_HOME`,
`GP_PI_DELEGATE_STATE` and `PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR` point into the state
volume; `GH_CONFIG_DIR` is pinned back to the shared volume so moving
`XDG_CONFIG_HOME` does not move the login out of it. `HERDR_CONFIG_PATH` still
points at the shipped `/etc/gp-pi/herdr/config.toml`.

The default instance deliberately does not set
`PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR`, so its pi sessions stay where pi has always
looked for them, in the shared volume. Every named instance sets it, so a named
instance never reads the default's sessions and the default never reads a
named one's.

**Labels are the registry.** `gp-pi.instance`, `gp-pi.workspace` and
`gp-pi.ports` are container labels. `gp-pi list`, lookup and status read them
back rather than a file a container could write. An unlabelled `gp-pi`
container is treated as the default instance with the legacy
`GP_PI_WORKSPACE`, so a pre-existing user keeps working without a recreate.
Labels cannot be added to an existing container, so migration is "treat it as
default"; the labels appear on the next recreate.

**Workspace guard.** On the physically resolved path, `$HOME` and any
ancestor, `/`, and the credential subtrees `.ssh`, `.aws`, `.gnupg`,
`.docker`, `.config/gh` and `.config/gp-pi` are refused. A workspace that
would contain or be contained by an existing instance's workspace is refused.
A non-directory is refused before a mount. The guard now protects `gp-pi
--workspace` and `gp-pi new --workspace`. `bootstrap.sh` no longer prompts for
a workspace or writes one, so its duplicated home and sensitive-subtree
predicates are gone with the prompt; the launcher remains the enforcement
point.

**Ports.** `--ports` and `GP_PI_PORTS` keep `3000` and `13000:3000`, and add
`:3000` to pick a free host port at or above guest 3000, skipping ports other
instances publish.

**Commands.** `gp-pi` attaches to the mountless default or a matching
workspace instance, `--workspace [dir]` and `--no-workspace` choose the mount,
and `new`, `attach`, `list`, `up`, `auth`, `shell`, `status`, `stop`, `rm`,
`recreate`, `build` and `help` round it out. `status`, `stop` and `rm` take
`--all`. `gp-pi mount` and `gp-pi unmount` are removed; changing a workspace is
`gp-pi rm <name>` plus `gp-pi new <name> --workspace <dir>`. `rm` removes the
instance's state volume and never `gp-pi-home`. `--force` is required for a
running instance and warns when agents are live.

## What changed

- `bin/gp-pi`: bare `gp-pi` is the mountless default again, `--workspace
  [dir]` and `--no-workspace` are top-level flags, plus instance resolution,
  labels, the state volume and env, the extended guard, auto host ports, the
  new command surface, and the removal of mount/unmount.
- `bootstrap.sh`: the workspace prompt and the config write are gone, and with
  them the duplicated home and sensitive-subtree predicates. The first-run
  default is mountless.
- `.github/scripts/check-launcher.sh`: checks for the mountless default, the
  `--workspace` and `--no-workspace` flag dispatch, attach-before-default, the
  `--workspace` refusals and idempotence, on top of the existing coverage.
- `.github/scripts/check-image.sh`: a state-volume override so the image check
  is hermetic and cleans up its own volume.
- `README.md`, `docs/design.md`, `docs/plan.md`.

## Verified

Without Docker, on Linux with bash 5.2.15:

- `.github/scripts/check-launcher.sh`: 190 checks, 0 failed. The new checks
  assert the mountless default (a configured `GP_PI_WORKSPACE` is not mounted),
  that `--workspace <dir>` mounts the directory and derives the instance name,
  that the cwd form resolves through `workspace_from_cwd`, that a second
  `--workspace` run attaches rather than creating, that `--no-workspace`
  creates the default and never a scratch instance and mounts nothing at
  `/work`, that the home, credential and overlap refusals fire on the
  `--workspace` path, and that an existing workspace instance wins over the
  default. The `--workspace` and `--no-workspace` top-level blocks are run
  through the real definitions with a stubbed docker.
- `.github/scripts/check-delegate.sh`: 182 checks, 0 failed (unaffected).
- `.github/scripts/check-shell.sh --syntax-only`: clean. shellcheck is not
  installed in this sandbox.
- `.github/scripts/check-conventions.sh`: clean.
- `bash -n bin/gp-pi bootstrap.sh`.
- `bin/gp-pi help` runs the top-level config parsing, port validation and
  workspace guard.

## Could not verify

This sandbox has no Docker daemon and no container to create, so the following
are reasoned about and covered by the unit-level tests, but not exercised
against a live daemon:

- two instances running at once, each mounted only at its own `/work`, and an
  agent in one unable to read the other's workspace;
- the per-instance state volumes actually separating pi sessions, herdr
  sessions and delegate records at runtime;
- the state-volume chown leaving `/home/pi/.state` writable by `pi`;
- `gp-pi list` reading labels back from a live daemon;
- `gp-pi rm --all` removing state volumes and leaving `gp-pi-home`;
- an existing single-container user unaffected end to end, including a legacy
  `GP_PI_WORKSPACE` still describing and attaching to their default container;
- a `gp-pi --workspace` run creating a real bind mount;
- the macOS/colima behaviour of all of the above.

These need a run on macOS with colima, which is the only platform here with a
Docker daemon. CI will cover the image build and the model/extension
invariants, but nothing in CI opens two consoles.

## Notes for review

- The default instance keeps pi sessions in the shared volume on purpose. It is
  the one place where the uniform rule is relaxed, and it is what makes the
  change backwards compatible. A deferred decision records migrating it later.
- `GP_PI_WORKSPACE` is now read only as the legacy workspace of a default
  container created before the instance labels, so an existing user's mount is
  still described and attached to correctly. It no longer drives the default
  create path.
- `gp-pi rm` removes the state volume, so a remount loses that instance's pi
  sessions. That is the trade the command surface chose, and the confirmation
  says so.
- `gp-pi recreate --all` does not exist; picking up an image bump means
  recreating each instance. Recorded in the deferred decisions table.
